subject: knitr workflow for a book project allowing \includeonly

messages.author: 467324c7303934a0
messages.subject: knitr workflow for a book project allowing \includeonly
parts:
I'm starting on a new edition of a book originally in straight latex, but now using knitr.  The original top-level file, book.tex
has the structure below, where chapters, ch1.tex, ... are input by \include{ch1} ... and I used \includeonly{} to restrict
processing to just those chapters mentioned.

I was planning to convert book.tex to book.Rnw, and each chX.tex to chX.Rnw, but I'm not sure how this works with
\includeonly{}, or whether there is a better organization to make it easy to work on a subset of chapters at a time.
Is there some example of a similarly organized book project using knitr I could follow?


%% ------------- book.tex -------------------
\documentclass[11pt]{book}
\usepackage{array}            %% nicer arrays and tables
\usepackage{times}            %% PS Times, rather than CM fonts
\usepackage[T1]{fontenc}      %% for non-alpha chars in \tt
\usepackage{sfheaders}        %% Chap/Sec headers in Helvetica
\usepackage{graphicx}         %% well, its about graphics
...
\includeonly{ch1,ch2,ch3}
...
\begin{document}
%% ============ Front matter ================
\frontmatter
\include{front}
\include{toc}
\include{preface}
%% ============ Main matter ================
\mainmatter
\pagenumbering{arabic}
\include{ch1}
\include{ch2}
\include{ch3}
\include{ch4}
\include{ch5}
\include{ch6}
\include{ch7}
...
\end{document}

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr workflow for a book project allowing \includeonly
parts:
Thanks;  I'm familiar with parent and child documents, and the demo you cite suggests to replace

\include{ch1}

with something like
<<ch1, child='ch1.Rnw', eval=TRUE>>=
@

But, for ongoing work, I'd like to be able to include these conditionally, which is what the LaTeX \includeonly{}
mechanism allows.  Maybe there is another way to do this with knitr, so that
(a) all the LaTeX definitions in my top-level book file are available in the child chapters, and
(b) I can work on and view one or more chapters at a time.

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr workflow for a book project allowing \includeonly
parts:
Since you have a copy of the knitr book -- I mentioned this very
briefly in the end of Section 12.1.3 (page 111). You can conditionally
include child documents using an if clause:

<<ch1, child=if (FALSE) 'ch1.Rnw'>>=
@

All this was made possible by an ingenious suggestion from Baptiste in
the early stage of knitr.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knitr workflow for a book project allowing \includeonly
parts:
Yes, you can wrap it up as a function like

includeonly = function(file) {
includes = c("ch1", "ch2", "ch3")
if (file %in% includes) paste0(file, '.Rnw')
}

then

<<ch1, child=includeonly('ch1')>>=
@

Regards,
Yihui
